experience.title: Research Intern
experience.organization: Machine Vision and Intelligence Lab, NIT Jamshedpur
highlights: Steel defect classification on NEU-DET and SteelDefectX (1,800 + 1,631 images).

AMFF-CNN (MobileNetV2 + FPN): designed a 3.4M-parameter CNN that fuses multi-scale FPN features using channel/spatial attention and learned cross-scale weights; 92.95% macro-F1 on a leakage-free held-out split, Grad-CAM weak localization, 118 ms CPU inference; 6-variant ablation across 3 seeds (TensorFlow).

TinySteelLLM (Transformer, from scratch): converted ~30 handcrafted OpenCV descriptors (edges, GLCM texture, FFT, region stats) into short text prompts and classified them with a 2-layer, 4-head Transformer encoder trained from random initialization — no pretrained weights or external APIs (PyTorch).

SteelSense-BiLSTM: scaled this to 92 descriptors tokenized into ~94 tokens and a 2-layer BiLSTM with attention/max/mean pooling (1.75M parameters); 99.67% ± 0.23 on NEU-DET and 99.02% ± 0.40 on SteelDefectX (5 seeds), benchmarked against XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, MobileNetV3 and ShuffleNetV2; first-author paper under review.

experience.title: Web Development Intern
highlights: Developed the backend for a recipe discovery app with 5 REST endpoints for search, lookup, and auth (Node.js, Express).

Architected a hybrid search layer that queries an in-memory catalog, merges it with the external TheMealDB API, and caps results at 50 per query; lookups check local data first and fall back to the external API.
Authored a data seeding script that generates 2,500+ recipes in TheMealDB’s schema with a separate ID range, so local and external results share one response format and never collide on lookup.
Secured the API with stateless JWT auth (1-hour expiry), bcrypt hashing, duplicate-account checks, and email/phone login.
Built the React frontend with React Router (7 pages), protected routes for dashboard and profile, and a Context API auth store that keeps users logged in across reloads (React 19, Vite).

projects.name: QuickFix — AI-Powered Customer Complaint Management System
projects.best_for: Backend engineering, AI/LLM systems, distributed architecture
projects.why_it_stands_out: The most architecturally ambitious build: an async orchestrator runs category, sentiment and priority agents in parallel, drafts policy-grounded replies with RAG, and survives provider outages through a 3-tier LLM fallback.
projects.hardest_part: Keeping complaints flowing when a cloud LLM fails or hits its rate limit, while every reply stays grounded in the company's real policy rather than guessed.
key_decisions: Parallel category, sentiment and priority agents coordinated by an async orchestrator, instead of one general model doing everything in sequence.
RAG so replies are drafted from the actual policy, not from what sounds plausible.
A 3-tier fallback — Groq LLaMA 3.3 → Gemini 2.0 Flash (multi-key rotation) → local TF-IDF/TextBlob — so the system keeps working when a cloud API fails.
An in-memory cache for repeated queries, cutting API response time from 2.5 s to ~0.5 s.
projects.problem: Support teams are slow and inconsistent at resolving complex customer complaints across many policy edge-cases.
projects.what_was_built: A support platform where an async orchestrator runs category, sentiment and priority agents in parallel on each complaint, then drafts a policy-grounded reply using RAG. It handles English, Hindi and Hinglish.
engineering_details: Async orchestrator running category, sentiment and priority agents in parallel per complaint.
3-tier LLM fallback: Groq LLaMA 3.3 → Gemini 2.0 Flash (multi-key rotation) → local TF-IDF/TextBlob.
In-memory cache for repeated queries cut API response time from 2.5 s to ~0.5 s.
REST APIs guarded by Google OAuth 2.0 + email OTP and JWT-based RBAC.
FastAPI, React 19, SQLAlchemy and Turso.

projects.name: Community AI Platform
projects.status: Live in production at communityai.co.in, used by 100+ active users
projects.best_for: Full-stack product engineering, applied AI, social-impact products
projects.why_it_stands_out: The project with the clearest real-world impact: a live platform used by 100+ active users to find 50+ government schemes, courses and jobs, with an AI assistant answering in 5 Indian languages.
projects.hardest_part: Designing the whole product around one question an ordinary user actually asks — 'what am I eligible for, and how do I get it?' — when the underlying information is scattered across dozens of sites, written in complex English and buried in PDFs.
key_decisions: A multi-model assistant (Amazon Q → Groq → Gemini fallback) so answers keep coming if one provider fails.
An automated content scanner so the catalogue updates itself from external sources instead of by hand.
Async FastAPI with background tasks, connection pooling and indexed queries so the backend stays fast under load.
JWT + bcrypt auth, Pydantic validation and rate limiting to keep the API safe.
projects.problem: Government help exists, but people never find it — details are spread across dozens of sites, written in complex English, and buried inside PDFs. Underserved communities can't discover the resources meant for them.
projects.what_was_built: A platform used by 100+ active users to find 50+ government schemes, courses and jobs, with an AI assistant (Amazon Q → Groq → Gemini fallback) answering in 5 Indian languages.
engineering_details: AI assistant with an Amazon Q → Groq → Gemini fallback, answering in 5 Indian languages.
Automated content scanner that pulls new schemes and courses from 2 external APIs (News, YouTube), adds them to the platform, and emails summaries via Brevo.
27 REST endpoints with async I/O, background tasks for email, connection pooling and indexed queries.
JWT + bcrypt auth, Pydantic validation and rate limiting.
FastAPI, React, SQLAlchemy and Turso.

projects.name: Steel Surface Defect Detection (AMFF-CNN)
projects.status: Ongoing research at NIT Jamshedpur; first-author paper (SteelSense-BiLSTM) under review at Discover Computing (Springer Nature)
projects.best_for: Machine learning, computer vision, research roles, edge deployment
projects.why_it_stands_out: The research project: three original models on NEU-DET and SteelDefectX, with the best (SteelSense-BiLSTM) reaching 99.67% ± 0.23 on NEU-DET and 99.02% ± 0.40 on SteelDefectX, and a first-author paper under review.
projects.hardest_part: Getting results that hold up — a leakage-free held-out split, ablations across multiple seeds, and benchmarks against strong classical and CNN baselines rather than a single lucky run.
key_decisions: AMFF-CNN: a compact 3.4M-parameter MobileNetV2 + FPN network with channel/spatial attention and learned cross-scale weights, evaluated on a leakage-free held-out split.
TinySteelLLM: describe each image with ~30 handcrafted OpenCV descriptors written as text, and classify with a small Transformer trained from scratch — no pretrained weights or external APIs.
SteelSense-BiLSTM: scale that to 92 descriptors (~94 tokens) with a 1.75M-parameter BiLSTM and attention/max/mean pooling.
projects.role: Research Intern — Machine Vision & Intelligence Lab, NIT Jamshedpur
projects.problem: Manual quality control on steel surfaces is slow, costly and inconsistent at spotting fine defects on a live production line.
projects.what_was_built: Three steel-defect classifiers on NEU-DET and SteelDefectX (1,800 + 1,631 images): AMFF-CNN (MobileNetV2 + FPN with attention fusion), TinySteelLLM (a from-scratch Transformer over descriptor text prompts) and SteelSense-BiLSTM.
engineering_details: AMFF-CNN: 3.4M parameters, 92.95% macro-F1 on a leakage-free held-out split, Grad-CAM weak localization, 118 ms CPU inference, 6-variant ablation across 3 seeds (TensorFlow).
TinySteelLLM: ~30 OpenCV descriptors (edges, GLCM texture, FFT, region stats) as text prompts, 2-layer 4-head Transformer encoder trained from random initialization (PyTorch).
SteelSense-BiLSTM: 92 descriptors tokenized into ~94 tokens, 2-layer BiLSTM with attention/max/mean pooling, 1.75M parameters.
Benchmarked against XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, MobileNetV3 and ShuffleNetV2.

projects.name: SOEIT Student Achievement Portal
projects.best_for: Full-stack engineering, role-based access control, product workflows
projects.why_it_stands_out: The clearest example of replacing a manual institutional process with software: three roles, a verification workflow, category-based point scoring with a weekly leaderboard, and one-click ATS resume export.
projects.hardest_part: Modelling one submission workflow that works for three different roles at once — students uploading, faculty verifying, admins managing — without the permissions leaking into each other.
key_decisions: JWT-based role access control as the organising principle — students upload, faculty verify, admins manage users and view analytics.
A stateless REST backend with SQL indexes, for sub-100 ms lookups on 10k+ records.
BLOB storage for certificates.
projects.problem: Student achievements are scattered across emails, spreadsheets and paperwork; students lose track of certificates and faculty spend hours verifying records.
projects.what_was_built: The achievement portal for Arka Jain University’s School of Engineering & IT: students upload certificates, faculty verify them, admins manage users and view analytics. Category-based point scoring feeds a weekly leaderboard, alongside a hub of 90+ curated hackathons and one-click ATS resume export (DOCX/PDF).
engineering_details: Automated category-based point scoring that feeds a weekly leaderboard.
Hub of 90+ curated hackathons and one-click ATS resume export (DOCX/PDF).
Stateless REST backend with SQL indexes for sub-100 ms lookups on 10k+ records.
JWT-based RBAC and BLOB storage for certificates.
Node.js, Express 5, React 19 and Turso.

projects.name: ArthaNova — Personal Finance Dashboard

Modular, scalable architecture designed for adding new financial features.

projects.name: Age & Gender Prediction
projects.why_it_stands_out: Shows a trained model turned into something that runs live on a camera feed, not a result hidden inside a notebook.
projects.hardest_part: Doing detection and prediction fast enough per frame to feel instant, while coping with varied lighting and face angles.
key_decisions: Haarcascade for face detection first — classic and very fast — so the CNN only ever sees a cropped face.
Optimising the loop for the speed/accuracy trade-off rather than chasing benchmark numbers.
projects.what_was_learned: How to balance speed against accuracy, and how much work it takes to move a trained model from test data to something that runs smoothly for a real user.
projects.problem: Biometric and analytics systems need fast, accurate age and gender estimation from a live camera feed.
projects.what_was_built: A real-time deep-learning app that detects faces with a Haarcascade classifier and predicts age range and gender with a CNN, drawing results onto the live video stream.
engineering_details: Haarcascade face detection per video frame before prediction.
CNN built and trained in PyTorch on cropped faces.
Inference loop optimized so detection and prediction feel instant on a live feed.

projects.name: Combat Online Plagiarism with AI
projects.why_it_stands_out: Attacks a loophole rather than a task: catching reworded plagiarism that literal text-matching always misses.
projects.hardest_part: Judging similarity by meaning rather than wording, so swapping 'big' for 'large' no longer defeats the checker.
key_decisions: Transformer embeddings so two sentences that say the same thing in different words end up with similar vectors.
Cosine similarity to score how aligned two ideas are, with high-scoring pairs flagged for a human to review rather than auto-judged.
projects.what_was_learned: How modern AI represents language as numbers, and how a simple, well-chosen mathematical comparison on top of those numbers can solve a problem exact matching never could.
projects.problem: Exact-match plagiarism checkers miss paraphrased or reworded content — swapping a few synonyms defeats them.
projects.what_was_built: An NLP system that converts text into Transformer embeddings and flags likely plagiarism using cosine similarity between meanings rather than literal text matching.
engineering_details: Text converted to vector embeddings that capture meaning.
Cosine similarity scores how aligned two pieces of text are (0 = unrelated, 1 = essentially identical).
High-similarity pairs are flagged for human review.
impact: Catches paraphrased plagiarism that literal matching misses

projects.name: Sentiment Analysis Pipeline
projects.why_it_stands_out: Ends at a decision, not a score: interactive charts let a non-technical reader see sentiment trends instead of reading numbers.
projects.hardest_part: Turning a mountain of raw opinions into a story a decision-maker can act on in seconds.
key_decisions: VADER because it handles everyday language including slang and emojis with no heavy training required.
Plotly charts so anyone can hover and filter — pairing a fast scorer with strong visualisation rather than chasing a bigger model.
projects.problem: Teams need to read sentiment across large volumes of text quickly, and see it rather than just score it.
projects.what_was_built: An end-to-end sentiment scoring pipeline using VADER with dynamic Plotly visualizations for fast, readable results.
engineering_details: VADER handles everyday language including slang and emojis with no heavy training required.
Automated ingest → clean → score → organize flow for large batches.
Interactive Plotly charts let non-technical users hover and filter to see sentiment trends.

projects.name: Black Friday Sales Prediction
projects.best_for: Classical ML on tabular data, feature engineering
projects.why_it_stands_out: Answers a concrete money question — how much will this customer spend — and covers the full data-science workflow end to end.
projects.hardest_part: Turning messy real sales records into features a model can actually learn from.
key_decisions: Pandas feature engineering to convert raw records (age, product category, past purchases) into clear signals.
XGBoost and LightGBM because gradient boosting handles complex patterns in tabular data particularly well.
projects.what_was_learned: The full workflow — cleaning, feature engineering, modelling and evaluation — tied to a business question rather than a benchmark.
projects.problem: Retailers lose money on both overstock and stockouts; the fix is forecasting customer spend in advance.
projects.what_was_built: A prediction engine using XGBoost and LightGBM to forecast customer spending behavior from historical sales data.
engineering_details: Pandas-based cleaning and feature engineering from raw records (age, product category, past purchases).
Gradient-boosting models (XGBoost, LightGBM) chosen for strong performance on tabular data.
Full data-science workflow: cleaning, feature engineering, modelling, evaluation.

Tailwind for a consistent design system and the dark/light theme.
Framer Motion for entry animation, GSAP ScrollTrigger for scroll reveals, React Three Fiber for the 3D layer.
A FastAPI backend for the AI chat, with answers grounded strictly in a validated profile file.

projects.what_was_built: A React + Vite portfolio with Tailwind CSS theming (dark/light), Framer Motion and GSAP scroll animations, genuine 3D particle backgrounds via React Three Fiber, and an interactive skill explorer, plus this AI chat representative.
engineering_details: Component-driven React architecture built with Vite for optimised production bundles.
Tailwind CSS design system with a dark/light theme toggle.
Framer Motion for entry/modal animation, GSAP ScrollTrigger for scroll reveals.
React Three Fiber / Three.js for 3D visuals without hurting page performance.
